What the numbers say

The actions column is what makes the row 130 pixels tall

Four controls stacked in one cell — the pen, Retire, Clear progress, Clear plan — on every row. The People register, which already has the three dots, runs at 39px.

130 → 51pxa row
1338 → 535pxthe table
2265 → 646pxthe whole page
1285 of 1285table width in the pane — no sideways scroll

Measured at 1560px in the demo tenant’s ten units. The page falls by a screen and a half because the second table — Unit marks, 705px repeating all ten names — goes with it.

Before you say yes

What this costs, and the three calls that are yours

What it costs

  • The Unit marks section goes, and its paragraph about PNG and transparency moves into the dialog. Uploading a mark becomes two presses (three dots → Replace the mark) where today it is one, on a page you had to scroll to reach.
  • Editing moves off the row. Correcting ten code prefixes becomes ten dialogs rather than ten pens in place. The register made this trade and it was the right one, but it is a real change to how a bulk tidy-up feels.
  • Functions gains a second way to edit unless its “Edit this row” becomes “Edit details” and opens the same dialog. I would do both, or the two neighbouring pages disagree about what editing means.

Three things I need from you

  1. Shown in the nav leaving the table. It becomes a grey note in the unit’s own cell, and only where the short name differs from the full one. That is the 159px that pays for the Mark column and the three dots without the table starting to scroll sideways. If you want the column kept, something else has to go — tell me which.
  2. The group’s Performance page can already arrange these same cards. After this there are two doors onto one list. I would leave it — it is the same list and the group page arranges themes and capabilities the same way — but say if you want it removed there.
  3. Companies. You did not ask, and its table has the same stacked-actions shape as Business units. It has no navigation order of its own, so it would get the three dots and no dragging. In or out?

What I would build on your yes

  • Business units: the table above, the dialog, the menu, and Arrange.
  • Functions: Arrange, and “Edit details” opening the same dialog.
  • A check that presses every control and reads the stored order back — run against today’s build first, so it is proved able to fail before its green is believed.
  • No migration, no schema change, no server change. The order is already a stored column and the server already calls a change to it the office’s.
